_comment: Signed risk acceptances for vulnerability findings that have no available fix.
This file is NOT a suppression list. An entry here changes one specific
finding from `failed` to `accepted`, and nothing else: a different
advisory, a different package, or a second high finding in the same package
still fails the gate. Every entry must carry an approver, a date, a
reachability argument and an expiry, and the gate fails when an entry is
expired, when required fields are missing, or when an entry no longer
matches any reported finding (stale entries fail, so an acceptance cannot
outlive the problem it was written for).
`expires_on` may not be more than MAX_ACCEPTANCE_DAYS in the future.
Raising this file's ceiling is a reviewable diff like any other.

acceptances.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
reachability: Build-time only. The sole consumer is chokidar's file watcher; `grep -rl chokidar` returns 0 files across apps/web/dist, apps/admin/dist and apps/jbrowse/dist.
The literal string `braces` does appear in those bundles, in exactly one place per bundle: React's own error text, "Did you forget to wrap your children in braces?". It is not the braces package.
Exploitation requires an attacker to control a brace pattern fed to brace expansion during a build. No such input crosses a boundary in this repository.
acceptances.rationale: braces 3.0.3 is the newest release; the advisory declares no patched version, so no upgrade, no lockfile change and no pnpm override can clear it. The alternative is removing Umi Max from three applications, which is a larger change than the risk. Accepted with the reachability above, on the understanding that it expires and must be re-reviewed.
acceptances.review: Re-check whether braces has shipped a fixed version, and whether umi/chokidar can be replaced without dropping Umi Max.
